releases.name: Relay 0.2.2
releases.body:
## Install or update

```sh
opencode plugin add relay-opencode@0.2.2
```

Updating from an earlier version: remove it first, because `plugin add` adds a second entry instead of replacing the first.

```sh
opencode plugin remove relay-opencode@0.2.1
opencode plugin add relay-opencode@0.2.2
```

With OpenCode Desktop only, run Desktop's own command-line binary the same way (on Windows `%APPDATA%\ai.opencode.desktop\cli\<version>-x64\opencode-cli.exe`). Then quit OpenCode completely and open it again. Your Relay settings are kept. To install with an AI coding agent, give it this repository's link and ask it to follow "Instructions for AI agents" in the [README](https://github.com/AsadKhalil/relay-opencode#install-with-an-ai-agent).

## What's new since 0.2.0

- **The panels, redesigned.** Relay's side panel is now a board of flight strips. Each mode (Plan, Execute, Review) is a bay. Each model you chose is a strip with its slot (1 is the default), model and provider, and its price (input over output), index and context printed beside it, then its effort and its "use it for" line. The decider is strip D, with its last choice and a box to try a message. A 7-day cost strip opens the usage tab. The long explanations moved into drawers, and Recent choices is one line per choice. A model OpenCode no longer offers is pulled aside with a stamp that says how to fix it. The usage tab follows the same design. Both panels follow Desktop's light or dark theme.
- **Prices, context and index for every provider and effort.** Each model's price is OpenCode's own, else $0 for a model that is free by its name, else Artificial Analysis's (with your key), else OpenRouter's public list (marked `*`, source on hover). Context comes from OpenCode, else OpenRouter. The index is the chosen effort's own score where Artificial Analysis lists it, else the highest effort's, else OpenRouter's copy. One matcher finds models across every list and provider: by name, without a date, with the words in another order, or by a unique ending. Claude through a Claude login now shows prices and an index.
- **Hints where no list has an index.** "Likely below" or "likely above" a newer or older version of the same model, else the range of models at about its price, else the reason there is none. Hints are never shown as a plain number, and Relay never ranks by them.
- **Usage.** Replies kept before you saved an Artificial Analysis key are priced when the usage tab reads them. A free model never borrows the paid model's price.
- **The Relay version** is shown beside Refresh.
- 0.2.1 (README only) brought the one-command install and agent steps that work with OpenCode Desktop and no `opencode` command.

## Tested

- 325 unit tests, and the isolated real-OpenCode smoke on OpenCode 2.3.0 (Windows; Linux, macOS and Windows in CI).
- The price, context and index matching ran on a real list of 123 models from four providers (OpenCode Zen, OpenCode Go, Ollama Cloud, Claude through a Claude login) at every effort: a price for 121, a context for 123, an index for 71. The rest are in no list and get a hint.
- The redesigned panels were checked in a preview with sample data, in day and night, by a separate review pass.

## Known limits

- The redesigned panels have not yet been seen inside OpenCode Desktop itself.
- Built for OpenCode 2.3. On 2.4.1 it runs in Desktop, but the smoke's mock model does not, so the smoke still uses the 2.3.0 CLI.
- More in [what has been tested, and known limits](https://github.com/AsadKhalil/relay-opencode/blob/main/docs/status.md).

Full change log: [docs/implementation-progress.md](https://github.com/AsadKhalil/relay-opencode/blob/main/docs/implementation-progress.md)

releases.name: Relay 0.2.1
releases.body:
A README-only release: no code change from 0.2.0. It puts the newer README on npm.

- **One-command install:** `opencode plugin add relay-opencode@0.2.1`.
- **Update by remove, then add:** `plugin add` on its own adds a second entry next to the old one.
- **Agent install steps that work with OpenCode Desktop and no `opencode` command:** an agent uses Desktop's own `opencode-cli`, or adds Relay to the config by hand, and stops before touching a Relay installed from a folder.

Newer: [0.2.2](https://github.com/AsadKhalil/relay-opencode/releases/tag/v0.2.2).

## Install or update

In OpenCode's global config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`; on Windows `C:\Users\<you>\.config\opencode\opencode.json`):

```json
{
  "plugins": ["relay-opencode@0.2.0"]
}
```

Then quit OpenCode completely and open it again. Your Relay settings are kept. To install with an AI coding agent, give it this repository's link and ask it to follow "Instructions for AI agents" in the [README](https://github.com/AsadKhalil/relay-opencode#install-with-an-ai-agent).

## What's new since 0.1.0

- **The Relay usage tab.** Every reply of every chat, with Relay on or off, kept for 90 days as numbers only. Spent and tokens at the top, a chart by day, totals by model, the records, search and filters. Open it with **Open Relay usage** in the command palette, or **Open usage** in the Relay panel.
- **Relay chooses by itself inside a mode.** Put two or more models in a mode and write no "use it for" lines: Relay sends big, tricky or unclear work to the model with the highest intelligence index, and small work to the cheapest. The decision model also sees the task the chat is working on.
- **Mixed providers.** Each mode can use a different provider. In testing on six exercises, Claude through a Claude login planning and reviewing with a cheap OpenCode Go model building passed all six, with Go paying 89% less than one Go model for each mode.
- **Better placement of short follow-ups.** The decision model reads the end of the chat's last reply, so "Implement it." after a plan is placed by that plan.
- **Usage by model and prices.** What each model took and cost, with prices from Artificial Analysis for models OpenCode lists no price for (with your key). `/relay-stats` shows Relay's earlier totals in the terminal app.
- **Install for people and AI agents.** A pinned install, update and removal steps, and step-by-step instructions an agent can follow.

## Tested

- 300 unit tests; the isolated real-host smoke on OpenCode 2.3.0 (Linux, macOS and Windows in CI).
- Real chats in OpenCode Desktop 2.4.1 on Windows, on OpenCode Go and with Claude through a Claude login.

## Known limits

- Built for OpenCode 2.3. On 2.4.1 it runs in Desktop, but the smoke's mock model does not, so the smoke still uses the 2.3.0 CLI.
- More in [what has been tested, and known limits](https://github.com/AsadKhalil/relay-opencode/blob/main/docs/status.md).

Full change log: [docs/implementation-progress.md](https://github.com/AsadKhalil/relay-opencode/blob/main/docs/implementation-progress.md)

## What's Changed
* Feature pilot implementation by @AsadKhalil in https://github.com/AsadKhalil/relay-opencode/pull/1
